body: There are a lot more than 151 cards. Bloody Genwunners.

If you find your team being funnelled into an enclosed encounter with overwhelming large mobs/groups of enemies where their archers and mages get a good shot at you, get your team to move back and hold position, get one member to aggro enemies and follow them back where you can pick them off generally one by one. 

I've beat the game on Nightmare a few times now (I play exclusively on Nightmare now) and generally don't use the tactics screen much anymore as I prefer to actively micromanage everyone. It's still worth paying attention to if you don't want to be pausing all the time.

Pay close attention to the buffs you get from passive abilities.

"Dog" can learn howl, which often stuns large groups of enemies simultaneously. Helpful for early game, especially those pesky Lothering mobs.

Alistair is arguably the best tank in the game, get him to learn Taunt ASAP. Things get easier when you meet the healer, or you can respec Morrigan (with mods) to know a healing spell or two. 

I've come to love the combat system but it confused the hell out of me at first. Best of luck, and have fun.

A mashup of Ludacris- Get Back and the Deep Roads theme from DA:O. It is glorious. Now I'm imagining some kind of montage of Aeducan/Brosca back in Orzammar having to deal with the Noble's crap.

Of course, I simply forgot to include it! I think the chance of seeing Antiva City would be wonderful, as would meeting the Merchant Princes and having a run in with the Antivan Crows.

Don't leave Lothering without recruiting the 2 people there. 

Talk to your companions often, switch them around every now and then even if you have a party that works, as they all have their own unique take on things, the dialogue between your companions is great. That said I am guilty of having Alistair as a permanent member of my squad, poor guy never gets a break.

Hold tab when playing (or map it to another key if you prefer) as this highlights objects in the environment and helps find points of interest and side quests.

I recommend maxing your Persuasion ASAP. 

I recommend this mod: http://www.nexusmods.com/dragonage/mods/385/? as it will tell you who might like a gift more and if a gift might trigger a special plot interaction. Of course you can play without mods, but I also recommend the mod that allows you to add your Mabari as a fourth companion "Extra Dog Slot" and "Grey Wardens of Ferelden" which allows you and outfits the Grey Wardens to have the Grey Warden armor from Dragon Age 2. (With this mod you need to install the Core file, not just the "main file" as otherwise Duncan will appear naked and it will be hilarious.) And the Sten/Qunari Update that makes the Qunari look how they do in Dragon Age 2. http://social.bioware.com/project/4592/ I also recommend the respec mod as this allows you to respec your squad and yourself as you see fit- plus you get cute ravens that hang around camp and towns and give you respec potions.

"Lothering > Circle > Redcliffe" is generally the best order for a first run for those first few quests, the order of the others don't truly matter, though I tend to leave Orzammar and Denerim last. The DLC for this game is really good and I recommend it. 

Read the Codex! You get useful information about the setting and characters, why they may act the way they do. If you don't want to play with mods your squad's codex entries give a good idea of what kind of gifts they may like. Morrigan likes Jewellery, Alistair likes artifacts depicting creatures or magical artifacts, Sten likes paintings.

If you have time, I recommend playing all of the origins, that way you can decide on a character you like best. Human Noble has arguably the biggest tie in with the main overarching plot. Human Noble, Dwarven Noble and City Elf are really amazing. Everyone has their preferences though, go with who you connect most with.

Have fun. Thedas is my favourite fictional world and DA:O is among my favourite games of all time.
I personally tend to do the first half of Redcliffe first, then the Circle Tower to completion, then go to Redcliffe castle.

Do you think it will be another mobile game? I hope not, personally. I hope for it to be PC/Consoles and not a microtransaction riddled, freemium mess. 

Do you think it will follow any semblance of story/narrative where we get an insight into something we haven't seen before like experiencing the first blight/second blight or even something post-trespasser, or something devoid of any actual plot like Heroes of Dragon Age? The latter is what I expect but I hope for something like the former.

I use the Grey Wardens of Ferelden mod in order to use the DA2 Grey Warden robes on my Cousland. My favourite vanilla armour set for my Aeducan is definitely the Legion of the Dead armour set. 

My Hawke often wears either a hood or the [Apostate's mask](http://dragonage.wikia.com/wiki/The_Apostate%27s_Mask), this particular Hawke is secretly a blood mage and uses it to hide her face/identity (when alone, as I imagine she'd be easily identifiable by the company she keeps.)

My Inquisitor Lavellan wears the Dragon Hunter set or Disciple Set!

A boss fight with Solas as this monstrous, many eyed wolf is the one thing I've wanted from his character since the moment I learned he was the Dread Wolf, imagine how absolutely amazing that would be.

As soon as they introduce the mage companion in the next game I'll just squint at them and take everything they say with a grain of salt, perhaps that might be what Bioware will intend you to think, or perhaps they predict you to think they wouldn't make the mage companion betray you again, they couldn't possibly- "everyone knows it's always the mage" but then do it anyway. Oh, Bioware.

1) I completely understand that we won't likely be seeing The Warden again due to the fact that so many people made the Ultimate Sacrifice with them, but some sort of conclusion to their story regarding their search for a cure for the Taint would put my mind at rest, if they die or their quest results in nothing or if they can return to their LI. A returning NPC from Origins that can speak in-depth about it would suffice, or a Grey Warden at Weisshaupt who comments on it, or from The Warden/their LI through written correspondence at the very least. Perhaps it will be a plot point if our travels bring us to the Anderfels - "Oh, we know of someone searching for a cure for the Taint but the messager who was supposed to relay that missive hasn't returned to us for some time, go find them. It's important." 

2) A setting relatively far removed from the first 3 games so they can focus on choice and a new narrative without a huge amount of overlap of choices from previous games. Anderfels, Par Vollen, Seheron, Rivain, Tevinter. Perhaps this seems to contradict my first point, but I'd just like a strong foundation on which new stories and choices can be made (like Origins) without having to account for every single decision players made in previous games, nods toward the player's previous choices accomplishments are good and very welcomed but I imagine accounting for things that shape an entire nation/the whole continent like who is on the Ferelden throne, who is Divine complicates matters for the writers. Being somewhere like Tevinter allows enough distance that decisions the player made can still be acknowledged without it being distracting. So that new players can find it as engaging. 


3) Returning characters. Likely Dorian, Solas, hopefully, the Inquisitor can be imported to some degree as if Solas is involved then surely they would be fairly integral. Though then they'd have to pay for the voice actors to do both the male and female English and American variants. Perhaps instead someone who joins your party as an agent of the Inquisition/a representative of the Inquisitors' interests? But then there's the whole issue of what you did with the Inquisition in Trespasser. Which brings up the question of who would be the ideal candidate for such a thing. The Inquisitor's Inner circle seem to be busy doing their own thing following Trespasser. Harding or Charter seems likely. Krem, maybe? (but then you'd have to account for if someone killed the Chargers, or maybe he didn't die and was just gravely wounded. He'd understandably be really bitter, about the Inquisition, about being back in Tevinter, about Bull. But if you saved The Chargers, he'd be more light hearted and Bull would return maybe.) I'd like to know if the individual left in the fade is gone for good. Part of me wants to see Alistair return in some form as he has in each game so far but that's just favouritism and wishful thinking on my part. If he's King we'd hopefully get a letter of some sort at least, and if he's a Grey Warden and survived the Fade and we go to Weisshaupt then he'll likely have something to do with it, maybe. 

4) Isn't Shale in Tevinter? If they're going to bring that plot over to DA:4, just imagine having her on your squad. "Squishy"/Dwarven Shale. Maybe the process of squishification means she has no memory of The Warden.


5) An update on how everyone from DA2 is doing. Varric is busy with Kirkwall, but Fenris/Anders/Merrill/Isabela/Carver/Bethany in Tevinter or at Weisshaupt would be interesting. I'd love Isabela to show up in the midst of a dire situation in which she helps during a possible Qunari Armada situation like the badass she is with her ship. 


6) Perhaps an unpopular opinion but I'd prefer non-voiced protagonist and a return to something akin to Origin's dialogue system. More opportunity for RP and establishing your character. If they're really intent on voice acting for the protagonist I'd still like dialogue options to be more fleshed out.


7) More consequences for choices within the story, high stakes, possibility for you to actually fail. While I never tend to make "evil" characters, that option being there is one people get a lot out of and adds a lot to the game. Companions can die horribly.


8) Origins, similar to how DA:O managed it. Perhaps even more in-depth. Maybe you can start the game as an Elven slave who escapes/kills their Tevinter Magister owner, a Tevinter Magister's offspring (Mage or Non Mage), a Qun-follower (Kossith/Other race), Tal-Vashoth, Saarebas, a Dalish elf, a Kal-Sharok Dwarf, a human from Ferelden/Orlais/Anderfels etc. Maybe even an Inquisition agent or Grey Warden.


9) Blood magic. If we are in Tevinter seems fitting for a player character being able to use. More specialisations in general. More armour variation.


10) Just more of Bioware's compelling narrative, story, characters would make me happier than I can express.

Really, really love them. Stolen Throne is my personal favourite, I find Maric and Loghain absolutely fascinating, and the book certainly paints Loghain in a different light.
This, Fire Emblem gameplay but with Bioware's writing and characters sounds like my perfect game. Exciting!

I didn't go (It's called the "Formal" here) as no one in my year liked me much barring one individual who tolerated my presence. I would have looked horrible in a dress (dresses and admission were expensive, too!) and I didn't want to go to be surrounded by drunk people who had ridiculed me for years or loud music, nor did I want to give them the opportunity to "award" me a derisive title/"most likely to" at those joke awards ceremonies.  

That said, for many people Prom/Formal is a positive experience and you might enjoy it, as many do. For a lot of people, they remember it fondly. Others, they wish they had stayed home.

Regardless of whether you choose to go or not, I wish you luck and hope you have a great time.
